Skullgirls Made a Small Change to Their Panties

I enjoy Skullgirls a lot, its actually probably the fighting game I've sunk the most time into besides Smash Bros.

I think that while these changes aren't necessary, they also aren't really a very big deal.

I didn't even notice the changes until this article pointed them out. We're talking about changes of like 3 frames of animation, stuff that gets lost in the action of the game itself.

If people are playing Skullgirls just for the panty shots they should just head to a rule 34 site. It's not like the characters depended upon flashing their underwear to determine the type of person they are, that's all covered handily in their voice lines and respective story modes.

Are they fixing something that isn't broken? Yes. Was it necessary for the game? No. But it doesn't affect the actual core of the game, a fighting game. If this was an h-visual novel, or a dating sim, or something along those lines. Then I could understand a bit of outrage from the community.

Then I could understand a bit of outrage from the community.

Personally I think getting on the case of 'Well this outrage is too much' is a bit of a red herring. Is the outrage too much? I'd say so, but fact of the matter is there's ALWAYS going to be someone upset by everything, and when we come to the internet those sorts of people are going to be able to get their outrage across to many more people.

There's ALWAYS going to be people who get way more upset then they should and take things way too far, I'm sure there are people who also go too far in support of the devs as well. Trying to measure if the outrage is 'justified' or how much of it is serves to stifle the discussion by making a bigger divide. As you pointed out they were fixing something that wasn't broken, theoretically that was time that could have been invested on different content to 'add' something to the game that wasn't already there (like work on a new character), given how at least according to the article it was only about 20 frames out of I believe 15,000 that got changed so I personally doubt they could have completed something entirely, but I won't fault people if they believe the time/energy could have been better spent elsewhere (even if they might be wrong), but by focusing rather on the people who take it too far (and there ALWAYS will be such people unless you manage to find a small enough group that no one disagrees) I imagine that you find 'less' value in such an argument then you potentially would have otherwise.

There will always be people who take things too personally and shout five times louder than someone more moderate, but focusing on their shouting as it is serves to do a disservice to whatever reasonable issues or discussion could be had, and it happens everywhere. I believe that it is best to do what you can to try to look past the outrage as it only serves to fuel an 'us vs them' mentality which hinders discussion and ideas.

But that's just what I believe.

Assuming the situation is as the article has described I personally will stand by the rights of the devs to change the game, at least in this instance, as long as they do not take active efforts to block mods designed to bring about the original animations in the 20 frames mentioned. Any efforts to block mods in general that may stop those sorts of mods well I would have issue with, but for unrelated reasons entirely.

And looking at the update to the article I don't exactly disagree with the sentiments that it appears that originally they had kinda gone out of their way to give panty shots, so I won't really fault them for changing their mind and thinking that perhaps it was a bit much, but all that said I personally have a bit less interest in them as developers for how they went about doing this. Like I said, I do believe it is their right but given the current climate of things I don't feel that their little joke or refusal to have any sort of discussion about this is really apt, I wouldn't call the changes they made to the game as 'censorship' because if things went down as the article describes it was merely those involved in the project utilizing their creative freedom to put out images that don't show off panties as much, which is well within their rights (though any sort of closing threads on steam or actively going out of their way to prevent discussion of this honestly small matter I would say is censorship). Part of what gives me a bit of an 'off' feeling when it comes to this is that I've just generally developed a bit of an aversion to people going out of their way to be 'politically correct', as more often then not they seem willing to sacrifice quality content for the sake of political correctness which generally offers little to nothing of value in of itself, so them putting in the time and effort to change up these frames (no matter how small) is essentially time/effort that theoretically could have been spent elsewhere, if these were the frames they had put out with the original content then I would still fault them for putting in the extra panty flashes when they could have potentially worked on other stuff (at least without making it an extra option). I also think that it would be nice if they would potentially have allowed players to have the option of which set of frames they get, because even though I agree that one shouldn't really be looking for porn directly from a game like this, it's still something that people might have enjoyed and I can't really argue for removing something that people enjoyed effectively for something that likely won't have a huge impact (people strongly against panty shots won't be happy if there are any in the game which disagrees with the idea that of course you'll see some, and this long after release the people who were just kinda uncomfortable with how many there were have probably long since forgotten about Skullgirls).

What's done is done though, while I personally have some concerns about some of the actions on the devs when it comes to this such as caring enough about something that's "not a big deal" (as some would say) to invest time/energy into it, telling people that there will be no discussions about it (even if they didn't say that, they wouldn't have to do what people said, but letting people vent goes a long way to helping to take the steam out of the outrage machine), and being a bit jokey about it just raises some red flags for me, maybe it's nothing but I personally will be taking a second look when it comes to these devs in the future. As it pertains to the fans who want to get those 20 frames back, I'm sure some people might still have some older versions of the game, potentially a mod or hack would be possible to be able to implement the old frames back in.

But those are just my thoughts.

My mom died in March and it was unexpected. It's rough. You won't grieve for the person 24/7 but you will grieve for them for the rest of your life. Nothing will change that. When it first happened, your brain has built in survival mechanisms for coping with the feeling of loss. When my mom died I mostly felt nothing. I would have periods of 5-10 minutes of sadness and crying followed by hours of no emotion. Your brain cuts off the sadness when it gets to be too much as a way to allow you to do what you need to do to keep surviving. As the days pass you compartmentalize the thoughts about the lost loved one off into a little room in your head. It's always there, but you can keep the door closed on it when you need to. You will open the door every once in a while and grieve and sometimes other things will force the door open for a while. For example, I recently moved to a new house and when I was packing I came across some old pictures of my mom and I was done packing for the day.

You will be happy again, you will move on with your life, but you will not leave the ones you lost behind. They sadness will be with you always and it will never be any less sad or make you feel less sad, but it won't always be present in the front of your mind and you will be able to do stuff without thinking about it. Your brain will section it off for you. It happens automatically, I think it's a natural biological process but I am not sure.

Just don't keep the door closed too much or you will start to forget things about the person and that will hurt, too. Also, try not to beat yourself up over any guilty feelings you have like not spending enough time with the person or calling them enough. There is nothing you can do about it.
